newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russians distrust Yeltsin but like some measures.
newsitem.headline: Russians distrust Yeltsin but like some measures.

text.p: Most Russians distrust President Boris Yeltsin but back some of his recent policy decisions, according to an opinion poll published on Thursday.
Interfax news agency said the poll, conducted in late May among 1,500 rural and urban Russians, showed that only 15 percent of respondents trusted Yeltsin, while 63 percent did not.
It was a part of a research programme run by the respected Obshchestvennoye Mneniye (Public Opinion) foundation.

Interfax said the latest figures indicated a slight fall in Yeltsin's popularity. Similar polls last autumn, soon after Yeltsin won a second term in office, gave him the trust of 18 percent of respondents.
But a majority of respondents backed a string of steps taken by the president to sort out painful political problems facing Russia and ensure its long-term stability.
The poll showed that 82 percent supported Yeltsin's order to Russian officials to declare their income and property, issued last month as part of an anti-corruption campaign.

Seventy-nine percent backed Yeltsin in signing a deal on loose union with neighbouring Belarus in late April, and 75 percent came out in favour of a peace treaty with the rebel region of Chechnya, which was signed in early May.

Interfax quoted Obshchestvennoye Mneniye experts as saying that the dramatic difference between general distrust of Yeltsin and the warm welcome for some of his policies could be explained by the lack of progress in economic issues seen by many Russians as most crucial to their well-being.
